title: De consolatione philosophiae
author: Boethius

passages.original: Minime, inquit, ludimus remque omnium maximam dei munere, quem dudum deprecabamur, exegimus. Ea est enim divinae forma substantiae, ut neque in externa dilabatur nec in se externum aliquid ipsa suscipiat, sed, sicut de ea Parmenides ait, πάντοϑεν εὐϰύϰλου σϕαίϱης ἐναλιγϰιον ὄγϰῳ
passages.english: "Not at all," she said, "are we playing games; and by the gift of God, whom we were entreating a little while ago, we have accomplished the greatest matter of all. For such is the form of the divine substance that it neither slips away into things outside [itself] nor itself takes anything external into itself; but, as Parmenides says of it, [it is] 'like the mass of a sphere well-rounded on every side.'"
passages.notes: The Greek quotation is from Parmenides (fr. 8.43); the printed Greek shows scanning distortions (e.g. ἐναλιγϰιον for ἐναλίγκιον), translated in the evident sense. The speaker is Philosophy, hence 'she'.
